parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A photon has an energy of 3.11 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

Calculate the momentum of the photon.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: A laser beam has a power of 350 mW. The light from the laser has a wavelength of 640 nm.
parts.text: Determine the number of photons emitted by the laser in a time of 1.0 s.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The laser beam is incident normal on a surface that absorbs all of the photons.

Show that the force *F* exerted on the surface by the laser beam is given by

*F* = *P*/*c*

where *P* is the power of the laser beam and *c* is the speed of light.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
Light of a single wavelength is incident on the surface of different metals. The work function energy of the metals is given in Table 7.1.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: For the metals in Table 7.1, calculate the value of the largest threshold wavelength.

figures.caption: Table 7.1
figures.alt: A table with columns headed “metal” and “work function energy/eV”, listing tungsten as 4.49, magnesium as 3.68, and potassium as 2.26.
